name: Docker
description: Docker is a platform for "accelerated container application development," providing tools to build, ship, and run containerized applications with security and isolation.
best_for: Docker serves individual developers (free Personal tier) up through Pro, Team, and Business/enterprise tiers; the site states 91% of Fortune 100 companies run on Docker and 20M+ developers build on it daily.

tiers.name: Personal
tiers.notes: Free forever. 1 Docker Scout-enabled repo, 1 private Hub repo, 100 Hub image pulls per hour.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.notes: $11/user/month billed monthly, or $9/user/month if billed annually. Unlimited Hub pull rate, 200 Build Cloud build minutes/month, 5-business-day support SLA.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.notes: $16/user/month monthly, $15/user/month if billed annually. Capped at up to 100 users. Adds RBAC and audit logs, 2-business-day support.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.notes: Flat $24/user/month — no discount for annual billing, unlike Pro and Team. Unlimited users, SSO/SCIM, invoice billing, 1-business-day support.

cons: Business is the only tier with no annual-billing discount — it's a flat $24/user/month either way, while Pro and Team both drop when paid annually.
SSO and SCIM provisioning are gated behind the Business tier, and even RBAC and audit logs require Team ($16/mo) — small teams on Pro ($11/mo) get none of these controls.
Team is hard-capped at 100 users; scaling past that forces a jump to Business at $24/user/month, a 60% per-seat increase over Team's annual rate, just to remove the seat cap.
features: Docker Hub for discovering/sharing container images
Docker Hardened Images (SLSA Level 3 patched images)
Docker Sandboxes (microVM isolation for AI agent sessions)
